newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - Politicians' comments on UK election.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Politicians' comments on UK election.

text.p: Following is a selection of comments from politicians on the outcome of Britain's May 1 parliamentary election, made as results were announced.
2115 GMT -- MICHAEL PORTILLO, DEFENCE MINISTER ((after exit polls pointed to massive Labour majority)
"The (Conservative) party has done itself no good by showing its divisions...Parties do better when they are not divided and that's something the party needs to address."

"We had one or two disagreements on the (European) single currency and I think that matter made it more difficult to be a credible party presenting ourselves to the public. Whatever the result may have been tonight, I am sure we could have done better had that not been so."
2120 GMT -- PADDY ASHDOWN, LIBERAL DEMOCRAT PARTY LEADER
"I would caution against predicting the results...I think we will see a strengthened position for the Liberal Democrats."
2115 GMT - JOHN PRESCOTT, LABOUR PARTY DEPUTY LEADER

"To win will be sufficient, make no mistake about that. We have to wait and see. To win is important and it looks as if we are going to win in very good fashion indeed...It is a remarkable testament to the courage and vision of Tony Blair...it was a tremendous organisational effort," he told the BBC.
BRIAN MAWHINNEY, CHAIRMAN OF CONSERVATIVE PARTY
"The people have already decided...we don't know the judgment they have passed and I am happy to wait until that becomes clear".
"I think we should wait until all of those ballot papers are counted. I don't think this is the moment to start reflecting on the campaign...There will be time enough to reflect in due course."
